First, since ${v}_{1}+{v}_{2}=0,$ we have that 

$$
\begin{aligned}9{v}_{1}-4{v}_{2} & =13{v}_{1}-4{v}_{1}-4{v}_{2} \\  & =13{v}_{1}-4({v}_{1}+{v}_{2}) \\  & =13{v}_{1}-4(0) \\  & =13{v}_{1}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
T(9{v}_{1}-4{v}_{2})=T(13{v}_{1}).
$$

Now, since $T$ is a linear transformation, we have that $T(kv)=kT(v).$ So 

$$
\begin{aligned}T(13{v}_{1}) & =13T({v}_{1}) \\  & =13[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 5 \\ -6\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-26 \\ 65 \\ -78\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

In conclusion, $T(9{v}_{1}-4{v}_{2})=[\begin{aligned}-26 \\ 65 \\ -78\end{aligned}].$
